summary:
Deep-space missions to Mars face a 20+ minute communication delay, meaning astronauts cannot wait for Earth to diagnose medical or radiation emergencies. A.R.E.S. (Autonomous Risk Evaluation System) is a delay-tolerant, autonomous medical triage console that empowers astronauts to act as their own first responders.

Instead of passive vitals tracking, A.R.E.S. targets high-risk deep-space hazards mapped directly to the NASA Human Research Program: Spaceflight Associated Neuro-ocular Syndrome (SANS), immune reactivation, and vestibular decline.

We integrate the live NASA DONKI API to detect Solar Energetic Particle storms, and calculate real-time Earth-Mars orbital light-time delays to unlock Autonomous Mode. When anomalies are detected, the app prescribes pre-authorized countermeasures (e.g., Thigh Cuffs), features an interactive 7x7 Amsler Grid, and uses a Hybrid Gemini/Offline Edge AI Flight Surgeon. Finally, it auto-generates a Ground Sync Summary for Earth downlink.
details:
How it works: A.R.E.S. is a delay-tolerant medical triage console. When an astronaut completes daily self-assessments (sleep, symptoms) and interactive tests (an Amsler grid for vision, a reaction-time test for vestibular function), our Svelte 5 rule engine evaluates the data.

Impact & Creativity: Deep-space missions to Mars face a 20+ minute communication delay. A.R.E.S. solves this by unlocking pre-authorized autonomous medical directives when Earth is too far away. We integrated live NASA DONKI space weather telemetry and calculate real-time Earth-Mars orbital light-time delay to trigger "Autonomous Mode." We also built a Hybrid AI Flight Surgeon (Google Gemini + Offline Edge Engine) so the AI works even during total comms blackouts.

Tools Used: Svelte 5 (Runes), Vite, Tailwind CSS, NASA DONKI API, Google Gemini API.
dataRefs: NASA Human Research Program (HRP) - 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight
